title: Power Apps: Power Apps CLI commands to find connectors and create connections for code apps
summary: Hold: the data-policy controls do not take administrators through to connector classification. The UI path stops at the policy list, and the PowerShell command creates a policy rather than assigning connectors to the groups that govern their use.

claims.claim: The environment toggle is at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Power Apps code apps > Enable code apps in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote:
Go to Manage > Environments > select the environment where you use code apps.
Go to Settings > Expand the Product subsection > Select Features.
Go to the feature Power Apps code apps and use the Enable code apps toggle to turn it on.

claims.claim: A runnable automation operation setting the code-app environment toggle is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerAppsAllowCodeApps" update environment API PowerShell; Power Apps code apps Enable code apps PowerAppsAllowCodeApps API update setting. Read SDK property and REST Update Environment Management Settings; no matching request-body property documented.

claims.claim: Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy is the complete path to the control deciding which connectors may be used or combined.
claims.quote:
From the list of data policies, select a policy, and then select Edit Policy.
Select the Prebuilt connectors step in the Edit Policy process.
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Block' and add to the existing note: 'The UI path blocks a blockable connector in an existing policy.' The cited page documents the Block action and explains that it is unavailable for unblockable connectors.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -DisplayName <name> -EnvironmentType <type> sets which connectors code apps may use or combine.
claims.quote: The New-DlpPolicy cmdlet creates a new DLP policy for the logged in admin's tenant.
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-guid> -Connectors <connector-objects> -Classification <General|Confidential|Blocked>' and docs with 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powerapps.administration.powershell/add-connectorstopolicy?view=pa-ps-latest'. Add to the existing note: 'Classification assigns connectors to Non-business (General), Business (Confidential), or Blocked; each connector object requires id, type, and name.' That reference explicitly documents moving connectors between groups; the current call only creates a policy.

claims.claim: Blockable connectors can be assigned to the Blocked group to prevent their use where the policy applies.
claims.quote: Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied. Unblockable connectors are in Non-business by default.

claims.claim: Data-policy connector groups govern which connectors can be combined in apps in the policy's scope.
claims.quote: By moving the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors to the Business data group, you're preventing users from creating flows and apps that combine these two connectors with any of the connectors in the Non-business or Blocked groups.

claims.quote: public bool? PowerAppsAllowCodeApps { get; set; }

claims.quote: Searched: "PowerAppsAllowCodeApps" update environment API PowerShell. Opened EnvironmentManagementSetting.PowerAppsAllowCodeApps Property in full; it contains the property declaration, type and package, not an update operation.

claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level data-policy procedures require Power Apps Environment Admin permissions outside the Dataverse exception.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: For environments with a Dataverse database, environment-level data-policy procedures require the System Administrator role instead.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.
